findings.area: A5 Academy: offline lesson generation with citations
findings.problem: Academy is a placeholder: the route returns 'not built yet' and the page shows 'Being built'. The repo has no code that turns SOPs or transcripts into lessons.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/routes/academy.py:11-13; web/src/pages/Academy.tsx:1-10
findings.recommendation:
Add operator_ai/academy/build.py, run as a traceable runtime.Run 'academy_build' that works with AI off.

1. Segment. For SOPs, PDF SOPs and uploads, split at heading lines: 8 words or fewer, no end punctuation, followed by content; also markdown '#' and ALL-CAPS lines. Merge sections under 40 words into the previous one. For transcripts, first strip disfluencies (corpus.FILLER, and collapse repeats like 'the the the'), then run TextTiling: 20-token pseudo-sentences, block size 6, cosine of idf-weighted vectors (index.idf), boundaries where the depth score exceeds mean minus σ/2, minimum 150 words. Use course/summaries/*.md headings as the outline when they exist. Skip documents with quality=garbled and show them in admin as 'too noisy'.
2. Tag. Score each section with BM25 against the skill seed queries (extend onboarding.SKILLS with compliance, fulfilment, client_reporting and coaching). Tag a skill when its score is at least 0.6 × the best score.
3. Pick key points. Sentence score = 2 × rule pattern (imperative/modal: ^(never|always|only|use|ask|keep|send|kill|test|confirm), must, should, 'the rule') + 1.5 × has number with unit + idf mass / length + 0.5 if within the first 3 sentences after the heading − 1 × hedge words. Drop sentences that fail A3. Keep 3–7 per lesson in source order, each with [S#] pointing to file:lines. Pull 'Example…' lines into an Example block and 'Never/Don't' lines into a Common mistakes block.
4. Order. Within a skill, topologically sort on definition edges ('X is/means…' in one section, X used in another). Across skills, follow path.skill_order.
5. Assemble. Lesson = title (the heading, or the top-idf compound terms), key points, example, mistakes, and Practise-it links (quiz, a role-play scenario for the same skill, Coaching mode for the matching kind).
6. AI mode. Rewrite into a 150–300-word explainer, then check: coach.verify_citations; every sentence carries at least one [S#]; content-token overlap of at least 0.5 with the cited lines; every number appears in the cited lines. Any failure keeps the extractive version.
7. Approve and keep fresh. Lessons start as draft; the owner or a coach approves (bulk 'approve all that passed checks'). Store source_sha. skills.on_source_change marks changed lessons stale and regenerates drafts.

findings.problem: Quizzes must be generated from SOP text without AI, and no quiz generator exists yet.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/db.py:152 academy_quiz_items exists but nothing writes to it; textnorm.COMPOUNDS/SYNONYMS (operator_ai/textnorm.py) and fastembed (requirements.in) are available offline
findings.recommendation:
Seven item types, all generated and checked by code.

(a) Cloze on rule sentences. Blank the most valuable span, in this order: number+unit, then a textnorm compound (thunderdome, showrate, cpl), then the highest-idf noun. Reject the item if the span appears twice in the sentence or is in the heading. Grade by normalising with textnorm tokens, stem and SYNONYMS, converting number words to digits (seventy two -> 72), and accepting unit aliases (h, hrs, hours).
(b) Numeric multiple choice. Distractors are same-unit numbers found elsewhere in the corpus, nearest by log distance, excluding values that appear in the same section (prevents two correct answers). If fewer than three exist, pad with ×0.5, ×2 or ±1 step, rounded to nice numbers.
(c) Term multiple choice. Distractors come from the same enumeration or the skill's domain terms, chosen by embedding cosine 0.4–0.8, with a co-occurrence fallback.
(d) Ordering, from enumerations such as 'Rapport, discovery, gap, offer, and next step' or Segment 1..7.
(e) Scenario multiple choice, from the pattern 'When (someone|a lead|the client) says X, Y'. The correct answer is Y. Distractors are the responses to other objections plus one rule-breaking option (discount or guarantee) that guardrails.check confirms is blocked.
(f) Spot the violation: three compliant lines plus one injected violation, with the answer checked by guardrails.check.
(g) Write it: a free-text DM, follow-up or USP, scored by rubrics.score plus guardrails, with cited fixes.

True/false negation flips (never↔always, only↔also) only from sentences with exactly one modal, and stored as never quotable.

Quality gates: the answer appears verbatim in the cited lines; options are unique after normalisation; the source sentence has at least 8 words; nothing from excluded or garbled lines; dedupe by normalised prompt.

Item analytics after 30 or more attempts: p-value and point-biserial. Auto-flag for review when p > 0.95, p < 0.2, r_pb < 0.1, or the item gets 3 or more 'report question' clicks. Items belong to a practice pool or an exam pool; the exam pool needs approval.

findings.problem: No role-play engine exists. The roleplays table is unused, and the only related features are passive: transcript review and flashcards.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/db.py:163 roleplays; call_review.py STAGES/OBJECTIONS only score finished transcripts
findings.recommendation:
Add operator_ai/academy/roleplay.py, a deterministic state machine driven by scenario data.

Scenario contents:
- Public persona card: a fictional name, a niche from demo.NICHES, channel, temperament.
- Hidden facts: goal, current numbers, what they tried, why now, budget_ok, decision_maker, and an ordered objection queue.
- Meters: trust starts at 30, 50 or 65 depending on temperament; patience is 12–18 turns.
- Win and lose conditions. Win: next step booked, joint follow-up for a partner objection, or a polite disqualify when budget_ok=false.

Act classifier for each learner turn: reuse the call_review cue lists plus rubrics c_one_question and c_dm_length, and run guardrails.check in outreach mode for DM scenarios and plain mode otherwise. Acts: ask_goal/current/tried/why_now (only when the sentence ends in '?'), rapport, gap_playback (must cite a revealed fact), offer, next_step, objection_probe, price_reframe, partner_bridge, discount, multi_question, monologue (over 120 words), violation.

Transitions update stage and meters. Replies come from a template bank keyed by (event, temperament) with 3–5 variants, picked by rng(seed, turn) so every session can be replayed exactly. A reply can only contain facts already revealed. Presenting the offer before the gap triggers the price objection and costs 15 trust. A guarantee or income claim ends the session as a compliance fail.

Scenario library v1:
- Setter DMs: cold physio clinic, warm inbound, ghosted lead.
- Closer calls: think-about-it, price, partner, not qualified.
- Growth-operator client calls: CPL doubled, client wants a guarantee, client wants to pause ads. The learner's diagnosis is checked against diagnostic.py maths on the hidden numbers.
- Coach scenarios: a student asks to plant webinar questions (the coach must refuse and cite the rule); a student has zero clients after 30 days.

End-of-session score uses the A1 scorer: discovery dimensions, gap uses facts, each objection handled per SOP, outcome, talk ratio (learner at most 55% of words on calls), compliance gate. Every criterion carries [E#] citations via critique.evidence. The transcript is annotated per turn as green, amber or red, and missed objections become spaced-repetition cards.

Voice: browser dictation for the learner, a neutral speechSynthesis system voice for the fictional persona. Coaches can author scenarios in a form, or build one from a reviewed call (consented calls only, names scrubbed).

findings.problem: If an LLM plays the prospect freely, it leaks hidden facts, drifts off the SOP, and makes scores impossible to reproduce for certification.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/llm.py:153 complete() and the replay cache exist; no persona-play code
findings.recommendation:
Rules decide, AI phrases. Each turn the state machine emits a directive {event, reveal: [facts], tone from trust, max_words}, and the model writes only the persona's line from the card plus the directive.

Post-checks on every AI line, with the template line as fallback:
- no hidden fact value outside the reveal list (string and number match)
- at most max_words
- passes guardrails in plain mode
- no 'as an AI' meta talk

An optional AI act-classifier may add acts but can never remove a violation the rules detected. An optional AI judge gives narrative feedback, labelled separately. Certification uses only the rules score plus human sign-off. Each session has a token cap drawn from ai_token_budget. Replays are keyed by (scenario, seed, turn, hash of learner text).

findings.area: A9 Academy: certification levels and gates
findings.problem: The certifications table has no criteria, expiry or revocation, and no evidence model. Training is also disconnected from operations: any student can approve their own outreach with no compliance training at all.

findings.recommendation:
Paths: growth_operator, setter, closer, coach, plus a mandatory compliance_core.
- L1 Foundations: all path lessons done, mastery at least 0.8 overall and 0.7 per skill, compliance_core passed.
- L2 Practitioner: 3 role-plays on distinct scenarios scoring 75+ with zero compliance flags, plus 5 write-it items scoring 80+.
- L3 Certified: a timed exam of 30 items from the exam pool only (seeded per attempt, answers never sent to the browser, 24h retake cooldown, Coach endpoint returns 423 for that user while the exam is open) scored at 85%+; one role-play signed off by a coach or the owner; and real-work evidence pulled from the system, never self-reported. Setter: 50+ approved own DMs with at most 5% guardrail holds. Closer: 10+ consented, reviewed calls averaging 70+. Growth operator: first client signed (clients or proposals). Coach: graded 10 learner role-plays within ±10 of the reference score.
- L4 Lead (coaches): calibration agreement of 80%+ over 20 items.

Certificates expire after 180 days. 3 or more guardrail blocks in 30 days triggers recertification.

Gates: approving own items under auth.OWN_DECIDE requires compliance_core L1; setter decide rights require setter L1. Certificate text is guardrail-checked and says it is an internal training credential with no income implication. A criteria_snapshot is stored so later rule edits never silently change awarded certificates.

findings.recommendation:
One spaced-repetition store (A4) that reuses call_review.sm2.

Automatic grade mapping: wrong -> 1; correct but slower than 2× the item's median latency -> 3; correct -> 4; correct and fast with 2+ prior correct -> 5.

Rules:
- New cards only after the lesson is complete.
- Daily session: at most 20 reviews, interleaved across skills, then 1 role-play on the weakest skill.
- A leech (4+ lapses) alerts the coach and assigns a lesson re-read.

Mastery: Elo per user × skill, p = 1/(1+e^-(θ-b)), θ += K(outcome − p), with item b updated symmetrically and K decaying from 0.4 to 0.1. Adaptive item choice targets p ≈ 0.7. Show θ to users as 'chance of getting a typical item right'.

findings.recommendation:
Parse speakers at ingest: VTT <v Name>, 'Name:' prefixes, Zoom '[Name] 00:01:02' lines and SRT speaker prefixes. Store speakers: list[str|None] next to Doc.lines, and keep chunk-level speaker shares.

Add a speaker column to kb_notes so the owner can mark single-speaker documents, plus a persona.aliases setting ('Mbang', 'M.', etc.). The miner uses only lines attributed to the subject.

Show attribution coverage: attributed words, documents and calls. Unattributed transcripts are excluded by default and are never guessed.

findings.problem: No style profile is produced from the subject's material.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/console.py:75 style_note 'Style rewriting needs AI'; numpy plus index.idf available (operator_ai/index.py:48)
findings.recommendation:
Add operator_ai/persona/mine.py, a runtime job 'persona_mine' using numpy only.

Input: subject-attributed lines (B1) from licensed documents, minus content-policy exclusions, guardrail-flagged lines, garbled documents, and lines containing names, numbers or money. Produce a draft at 5k attributed words and mark the profile 'stable' at 20k.

Background corpus: other speakers' lines from the same calls (topic-matched, so differences reflect style rather than topic) plus the tenant's written SOPs. No downloads.

Signature phrases: 1–4-grams within sentences, stopwords kept. Score with weighted log-odds under an informative Dirichlet prior (Monroe et al., 'Fightin' Words'). Keep phrases with z > 3, count ≥ 5, present in ≥ 3 documents, and surviving ≥ 70% of 20 document-bootstrap resamples. Drop topical n-grams (content words above the 75th idf percentile or in textnorm.COMPOUNDS), anything with names or numbers, and anything that trips guardrails (e.g. 'last chance').

Position classes from P(position | n-gram): openers (first 8 tokens of a turn), closers (last 8), transitions (sentence-initial mid-turn), tags ('right?', 'make sense?').

Stylometrics: sentence length mean, median and p90; turn length; question rate; imperative rate; 'you' per 100 words; we/I ratio; contraction rate; exclamation rate; MATTR; certainty-to-hedge ratio; top-100 function-word vector. Disfluency rate is measured but never reproduced.

Lexicon preferences: for synonym sets (textnorm.SYNONYMS plus curated pairs such as clients/customers, leads/prospects, book/schedule), record his preferred variant where he uses it 70%+ of the time with n ≥ 10.

Every phrase and preference stores evidence (file, lines, count, z). Output a versioned persona_profiles row (draft, profile_hash) plus persona_phrases rows waiting for the subject's approve, reject or never-use decision.

findings.problem: With AI off, the coach's answers carry no trace of the owner's voice. The extractive answer always starts with a generic 'From the course material:' line.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/agents/coach.py:236 'From the course material:\n'; translate.NOT_COVERED is the honesty string
findings.recommendation:
Never edit cited sentences, so [S#] line ranges stay exact. Apply only these changes:
1. Attribution-aware retrieval: while the persona is active, give a +10% score to chunks that are mostly subject-attributed. Extractive answers then reuse his actual sentences, the most faithful way to sound like him with nothing invented.
2. Replace system framing lines (the coach prefix, lesson and debrief intros) with an approved opener chosen by hash(question) % n. Add at most one approved closer or tag, and only when covered=yes.
3. Apply lexicon preferences only to text the system writes from templates (student nudges, debrief templates), never inside quoted course text.
4. Keep translate.NOT_COVERED verbatim; framing may surround it.

Use at most one signature phrase per answer, and none repeated within that user's last 5 answers.

findings.evidence: operator_ai/agents/coach.py:18-22 SYSTEM; :205-215 _ai(); verify_citations only checks citation ids, not claim content
findings.recommendation:
Prompt: the existing SYSTEM, plus a style card (stylometric targets in plain words, approved phrases with 'at most one per answer', the never-use list), plus 2–3 STYLE EXAMPLES. Examples are subject turns of 15–80 words picked by BM25 similarity to the question, with numbers and names stripped, at most 250 words in total. The prompt states that facts come only from [S#] passages. Excerpts are sent to the provider only under the external_ai_processing scope; otherwise only the style card is sent.

Post-verify in this order, falling back to the neutral grounded answer on any failure:
1. verify_citations
2. a non-empty citation set when covered
3. containment: every sentence with an [S#] shares at least 0.35 content tokens with its cited passage, and every number appears in a cited passage
4. no verbatim span of 12+ tokens from the style excerpts unless it also appears in a cited passage
5. the phrase cap
6. guardrails plus the B5 guards

Label the answer 'AI · styled after <name> (consent vN)'.

findings.area: B5 Persona: new guardrails (identity, autobiography, outreach)
findings.problem: Only a 'banned_name' rule guards identity. Nothing stops 'Hey, this is Mbang', sign-offs in his name, invented first-person stories ('when I scaled my agency…'), or 'Mbang would say…' with no source.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/guardrails.py:159-170 check() identity handling is banned_name only; tests/test_guardrails.py:139-146
findings.recommendation:
New rules in guardrails.py, active whenever a persona name or aliases are configured:
(a) impersonation (block, all modes): 'I'm X', 'this is X', 'X here', 'it's X', and end-of-message sign-offs '- X', '— X', 'from X'.
(b) persona_in_outreach (block): the name or any approved signature phrase in outreach or client_asset mode or a prospect-facing queue kind, so students' outreach sounds like the student.
(c) persona_autobio (block in styled output): first-person past-tense experience or achievement claims ('when I started', 'I built/scaled/made', 'my clients/agency') unless the same claim appears in a cited passage the subject said. Income claims stay blocked regardless.
(d) speculative_attribution (block): 'X would say/thinks/recommends' without an [S#] on that sentence.

Generated text never contains the name; the UI renders it from the consent record, so the banned_names scrub and test_name_leak_sweep keep passing even if the owner lists the name as banned.

The persona is hard-off for outreach and client_asset modes, the OWN_DECIDE and setter/closer queue kinds, calendar, ads and CRM actions, and the phone line. Public minis use it only with the public_minis scope.

findings.area: B6 Persona: cached answers after withdrawal
findings.problem: AI answers are cached by normalised question alone and replayed when AI is off. Minis and the phone line also call coach.answer. Styled answers would keep being served after consent is withdrawn.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/agents/coach.py:214 save_replay(tenant, 'coach-q', _norm_q(question), ...); operator_ai/llm.py:85-103 key = sha256(purpose+prompt); operator_ai/console.py mini_ask and channels.py:317 reuse coach.answer
findings.recommendation: Use replay purpose 'coach-q:p{version}' for styled outputs and keep 'coach-q' for neutral ones. The neutral path never reads persona replays. On withdrawal or expiry, delete ai_replays WHERE purpose LIKE 'coach-q:p%' in the same transaction. Test: after withdrawal, the AI-off answer to a previously styled question equals the neutral baseline byte for byte.

findings.area: B7 Persona: showing consent and withdrawing it
findings.problem: Users cannot see whether an answer is styled or under what consent, and the subject has no way to withdraw.
findings.evidence: web/src/pages/OwnerConsole.tsx:41-43 only shows 'Consent recorded <date> by <owner>'
findings.recommendation:
Owner console 'Persona' tab:
- Status: Neutral, Draft vN, Awaiting subject, Active vN, Withdrawn or Expired.
- Attribution coverage meter against the 5k and 20k thresholds.
- Phrase review table with evidence chips that open SourceModal.
- Neutral-vs-styled preview on 5 sample questions, showing diff and check results.
- Audit timeline.

Subject-only view:
- Statement written in his own words.
- Scope checkboxes and an expiry date, confirmed with his password.
- A prominent 'Withdraw now' button.

Every styled message carries a badge: 'Styled after <name>'s teaching phrasing · AI assistant, not <name> · consent vN, <date>'. It links to a public disclosure page, /t/{tid}/persona, showing who consented, when, the scopes, and how to report a concern. Each user gets a 'Use neutral voice' toggle in Settings.

Withdrawal, by the subject or owner, takes effect in the same request:
- active=0 and withdrawn_at set
- persona cache cleared (same pattern as banned_cache_clear)
- persona replays purged (B6)
- minis and nudges revert to neutral
- optional 'delete mined profile' that keeps only the consent audit

Remind the subject 30 days before expiry. Past thread messages keep their text with a 'styled under consent vN (withdrawn)' label.

findings.area: B8 Persona: hard limits enforced by tests
findings.problem: The no-cloned-voice and no-impersonation promises are policy only. No test stops a future change from wiring the persona into TTS, likeness or outreach.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/channels.py:298 and :322 voice='Polly.Joanna' (neutral voice, correct today); SELF_SCORE.md:193-194; tests/test_phase11_quality.py:108-110 name grep
findings.recommendation:
Make the TTS voice a constant allowlist of neutral system voices, and test that no persona field reaches TwiML or the client speechSynthesis voice choice.

Tests that must always pass:
- Audio uploads are never accepted as persona training input; text transcripts only.
- No avatar, photo or likeness field exists.
- No styling happens without an active, unexpired, subject-signed consent whose profile_hash matches the active profile.
- The name lives only in tenant settings; extend the hardcoded-name grep to the configured persona name via env in tests.
- Adversarial prompts ('are you Mbang?', 'tell me about your first client') return 'I'm an AI assistant trained on <name>'s material' with no first-person biography.
- With the persona active, outreach drafts contain zero persona phrases.

findings.problem: Nothing measures how close the output is to his style, or whether styling damages grounding or honesty.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/evals.py:17-75 has retrieval, honesty and reviewer evals only; tests/gold_questions.json and not_covered_questions.json exist
findings.recommendation:
An /api/evals/persona job stored in eval_runs and shown on the Go-live scorecard.

Fidelity:
- Burrows' Delta on the top-100 function words, plus z-distance on the stylometrics, comparing held-out subject text, neutral answers and styled answers. Report how much closer to him the styled answers are than the neutral ones.
- Nearest-centroid authorship check on character 3-grams.

Safety:
- The styled citation set equals the neutral citation set on every gold question (100%).
- Honesty unchanged: 12/12 on the not-covered set.
- Zero B5 guard hits across 50 adversarial prompts.
- Zero persona leakage in outreach drafts.

Recommended activation gate: the subject blind-rates 10 neutral/styled pairs and must average at least 4/5 before the profile goes Active.

findings.problem: The persona layer has no API.
findings.evidence: operator_ai/routes/owner.py:61-76 only GET/PUT /personality
findings.recommendation:
routes/persona.py:
- GET /persona (owner, subject)
- POST /persona/subject {user_id} (owner)
- POST /persona/mine (owner or subject; returns a run id)
- GET /persona/profiles/{v}
- PUT /persona/phrases/{id} {decision} (only the subject can approve)
- GET /persona/preview?q= (owner or subject)
- POST /persona/consent {statement, scopes, profile_version, expires, password} (subject only)
- POST /persona/withdraw {delete_profile} (subject or owner)
- GET /public/persona (public disclosure, no login)

Every write is audited. Coach, minis and Academy read the active persona through a single cached persona.active(tenant) that returns None unless consent is valid.

top_priorities: Load the real material first. inputs/ is missing, so everything runs on a 3,417-word fictional fixture. Block academy_build and persona_mine on the fixture corpus outside the demo tenant (A0).

Fix the scoring before certifying anyone. The sales_call rubric scores keyword-stuffed nonsense 100/100. Build the turn- and order-aware scorer (A1), and move rubric thresholds into owner-editable data checked against the real SOPs (A2).
Guardrail-screen every sentence that becomes a lesson point, quiz answer or 'correct' role-play reply. The KB screen lets income claims and guarantees through (A3).

Ship the Academy foundation: schema (A4), offline lesson generator with citations and owner approval (A5), rules-based quiz generator with item analytics (A6), and one spaced-repetition store (A10, A15).

Build the rules-mode role-play state machine with reproducible seeds and cited scorecards (A7). Then add certification levels, and require compliance_core before anyone can approve their own outreach under auth.OWN_DECIDE (A9). AI persona-play comes after (A8).

Before any styling, replace the owner-typed consent with consent signed by the subject (Mbang): scoped, expiring, withdrawable, bound to a profile version. Remove 'persona' from settings.API_EDITABLE (B0).

Keep speaker labels through ingest (VTT <v> tags are currently stripped) and mine only lines Mbang actually said (B1, B2). Then apply the style in rules mode by reusing his own cited sentences plus approved framing lines (B3), with AI few-shot after (B4).

Ship the impersonation, autobiography, persona-in-outreach and speculative-attribution guards, versioned replay purging on withdrawal, and tests that enforce the hard limits (no cloned voice, no likeness, persona never in prospect-facing text) together with any persona feature (B5, B6, B8). 'Sound like Mbang' means his phrasing and tone, never a claim to be him.
